question:
G protein-gated inwardly rectifying potassium (GIRK2) channels regulate neuronal excitability and are implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders. A rare KCNJ6 variant, G154C (hGIRK2G154C), was identified in a patient with mild Keppen-Lubinsky syndrome features, contrasting with severe phenotypes linked to other selectivity filter mutations.

Three candidate results follow. Exactly one is what this study reported.
- Result A: Here we combined molecular dynamics simulations and patch-clamp electrophysiology to characterize the hGIRK2G154C mutant, revealing a widened selectivity filter that resulted in loss of potassium selectivity, aberrant sodium permeation, and loss of inward rectification, indicating a severe gain-of-function phenotype. An in silico and electrophysiological drug screen identified FDA-approved compounds, including nefazodone and eletriptan, that potently inhibited GIRK2G154C but not wild-type GIRK2 through distinct blocking mechanisms. These findings elucidate the structural and functional impact of the G154C mutation and highlight mutant-selective pharmacological tools and therapeutic candidates for the treatment of GIRK2 channelopathies.
- Result B: Here we combined molecular dynamics simulations and patch-clamp electrophysiology to characterize the hGIRK2G154C mutant, revealing a constricted selectivity filter that reduced potassium conductance, prevented aberrant sodium permeation, and preserved inward rectification, indicating a severe loss-of-function phenotype. An in silico and electrophysiological drug screen identified FDA-approved compounds, including nefazodone and eletriptan, that potently activated GIRK2 and GIRK2G154C through distinct modulatory mechanisms. These findings elucidate the structural and functional impact of the G154C mutation and highlight potential pharmacological tools and therapeutic candidates for the treatment of GIRK2 channelopathies.
- Result C: Here we combined molecular dynamics simulations and patch-clamp electrophysiology to characterize the hGIRK2G154C mutant, revealing a widened selectivity filter that resulted in loss of potassium selectivity, aberrant sodium permeation, and loss of inward rectification, indicating a severe gain-of-function phenotype. An in silico and electrophysiological drug screen identified FDA-approved compounds, including nefazodone and eletriptan, that potently inhibited GIRK2 and GIRK2G154C through distinct blocking mechanisms. These findings elucidate the structural and functional impact of the G154C mutation and highlight potential pharmacological tools and therapeutic candidates for the treatment of GIRK2 channelopathies.
Which result did this study report? Rank the candidates, and give the mechanism, the key evidence, and a validation experiment for the top pick.
